To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
repeated exposure of a brain region that supports the reinforcing and dopamine stimulating effects of nicotine increases the sensitivity to the dopamine stimulating effects of alcohol.
repeated exposure of a brain region to one drug increases the sensitivity of dopamine neurons to the stimulant effects of the other, co-abused drug.
repeated exposure of pVTA to 100 μM of nicotine for 7 days increases the dopamine-stimulated response of local dopamine cells to the stimulating effects (200 mg%) of ethanol.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of repeated exposure to nicotine and ethanol on dopamine release in the nucleus accumbens.
the effects of repeated exposure to nicotine and ethanol in the pVT on the response of local dopaminergic neurons to the other drug.
understanding how exposure to one drug can increase the reinforcing and dopamine stimulatory effects of another drug.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
repeated exposure to nicotine increases the response of pVTA DA neurons to ethanol.
repeated exposure of a brain region to a drug can change the response of local neurons to the stimulating effect of other drugs.

repeated exposure of pVTA to a drug increases the sensitivity of the local dopamine neurons to that drug and possibly to the other drug, but that repeated exposure to a drug does not necessarily alter the sensitivity of pVTA local dopamine neurons to another drug.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
repeated exposure of dopamine neurons in the pVTa to one drug (nicotine) increases the sensitivity of the neurons to a second drug (ethanol), but not the other way around.
repeated exposure of a common neural substrate (pVTA dopamine neurons) to one addictive drug can alter the response of that same substrate to another addictive drug.
repeated exposure of a common brain area to two drugs of abuse increases the sensitivity of dopamine neurons to the stimulatory effects of both drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the pVTA is a critical brain area for the reinforcing and dopamine stimulating effects of both nicotine and alcohol and that the reinforcing effects of these drugs may interact in the pVta to produce a synergistic effect on local dopamine neurons.
repeated exposure to nicotine increases the response of local VTA dopamine neurons to ethanol, whereas repeated ethanol exposure does not alter the responses to nicotine.
repeated exposure of pVTA to either nicotine or ethanol may increase the sensitivity of pVTA DA neurons to the other drug.
